planting.note: Direct sow after all danger of frost has passed, spacing plants to allow branching, or succession sow every 1-2 weeks for a continuous cutting supply.

directions: Sunbright is a branching, pollen-free sunflower bred for the commercial cut-flower trade, producing clean golden-yellow petals around a dark center disc on multiple uniform stems per plant. Because it branches freely rather than growing a single giant head, one sowing yields repeated flushes of medium-sized blooms over several weeks, and succession sowing extends the harvest window further. The pollenless flowers won't shed onto tablecloths or clothing, making them a favorite for mixed bouquets, and the sturdy stems hold up well after cutting when placed promptly in water. Full sun and even moisture through establishment give the straightest stems and best branching.

common_name: Big Smile Sunflower (Dwarf Single-Stem Sunflower with Oversized Blooms)

planting.note: Direct sow after frost danger has passed; being a compact single-stem type, it does not need the wide spacing branching sunflowers require.

directions: Big Smile packs a full-sized, 4-6 inch golden flower head with a rich chocolate-brown center onto a dwarf plant that rarely exceeds 16 inches, giving it a deliberately top-heavy, oversized look that stands out in containers and edging plantings. Like other single-stem sunflowers it produces just one main bloom per plant rather than repeat side branches, so staggered sowings every couple of weeks keep fresh flowers coming through summer. Its short stature means it rarely needs staking even when the flower head is disproportionately large, and it performs well in pots where taller sunflower types would topple. Deadheading isn't necessary for more bloom since it's a one-shot flowerer, but spent heads can be left to dry for birdseed.

common_name: Double Dandy Sunflower (Dwarf Double Bicolor Pollen-Free Sunflower)

planting.note: Direct sow after frost danger passes into a sunny bed, border, or large container.

directions: Double Dandy bears fully double, ruffled flower heads that shade from deep red at the petal base to bright yellow at the tips, giving each bloom a fiery bicolor effect distinct from typical single-petaled sunflowers. Bred as a pollen-free ornamental type, it drops no messy pollen onto patios, porches, or indoor surfaces, and its compact, bushy 16-24 inch habit suits containers and border fronts better than tall field sunflowers. Multiple flowers open per plant over the season on a well-branched frame, so no staking is usually needed. Even light, well-drained soil and full sun keep the double blooms full and the plant sturdy.

planting.note: Direct sow after all danger of frost has passed, spacing plants to allow branching, or succession sow every 2-3 weeks for continuous blooms.

directions: Buttercream offers a soft, pastel departure from typical bold-gold sunflowers, with pale creamy-butter yellow petals set against a dark center disc. It branches freely, producing a steady succession of medium blooms on a single plant over several weeks rather than one large flush, which makes it useful for gardeners who want a long cutting season without repeated sowings. Its muted color pairs well with pinks, whites, and other pastels in mixed bouquets where classic bright-gold sunflowers would clash. Full sun and moderate, even watering through establishment produce the strongest stems and most prolific branching.

planting.note: Direct sow after last frost into average, well-drained soil in full sun; Cosmic Red is a compact, early-flowering selection that tolerates heat, humidity, and poor soil better than most bedding annuals.

directions: Cosmic Red is a dwarf, mounding selection of Cosmos sulphureus bred as a companion shade to Cosmic Orange and Cosmic Yellow, bearing deep red-orange single blooms above finely cut, dark green foliage on compact 12-18 inch plants. Its low, tidy habit suits front-of-border plantings, containers, and mass bedding where taller cosmos would flop or overwhelm. It begins flowering earlier than standard-sized sulphureus types and continues nonstop through summer heat into fall with no deadheading required. Like other Cosmic series selections, it is highly heat- and drought-tolerant once established and performs poorly in rich, heavily fertilized soil.

planting.note: Direct sow after frost in warm soil, barely covering the seed, and thin plants to 12-18 inches apart.

directions: Fizzy Pink is the pink-flowered companion to Fizzy White, bearing 2.5-4 inch semi-double blooms of pleated, zigzag-edged petals around fluffy tufted centers that give the flowers a distinctive frilled, textured look unlike smooth-petaled cosmos. This heat-loving annual attracts butterflies and other pollinators and makes an airy, long-lasting cut flower. Grow in lean soil with modest water, since rich, wet conditions favor foliage over flowers; deadhead spent blooms to prolong the display through summer into fall.
